extracted.intended_audience: chemical manufacturers, importers, distributors, label/SDS preparers, employers, and OSHA compliance stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Final-rule guidance and requirements for classifying physical hazards, allocating label elements, and preparing SDS information under OSHA's Hazard Communication Standard (HCS) as updated to align with GHS Rev.7. Includes specific Appendix B and C criteria and instructions for label and SDS content and testing/data use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate boiling point calculation for storage
rubrics_metrics.description: The flammable liquids standard permits use of an alternate calculation (§1910.106(a)(5)) to determine boiling point for selecting appropriate flammable liquid storage container size and type when an accurate boiling point is not available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This alternate calculation is solely allowed in determining storage requirements and would practically apply to Category 1 flammable liquid mixtures. If an alternate calculation is used for storage purposes and the resulting classification for storage differs from the classification listed in Section 2 of the SDS, the manufacturer, importer, or distributor must clearly note in Sections 7 and 9 of the SDS that an alternate calculation was used (example note: “Initial boiling point 80 °F/estimated boiling point 100 °F (for storage purposes)”). If the alternate calculation does not change storage classification, no additional note is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial boiling point testing standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial boiling point shall be determined in accordance with ASTM D86-07a or ASTM D1078.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA limited the calculation of boiling point to these two ASTM standards; comments seeking changes to this requirement were considered out of scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing references are permissive (no testing mandate)
rubrics_metrics.description: References to testing standards in the HCS state acceptable methods for determining characteristics but do not require the SDS or label preparer to perform testing themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classifiers may rely on acceptable methods or on data from the literature generated using specified or equivalent test methods; OSHA is indicating methods are acceptable, not imposing an obligation to test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnote supplemental information and GHS alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental information (such as noting an alternate boiling point calculation on the SDS) is permitted by the GHS and does not change ultimate classification under the HCS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA considers the alternate boiling point calculation supplemental; because it is not used in ultimate classification under the HCS it remains aligned with the GHS. OSHA added a footnote clarifying when alternate calculation may be used for storage and the SDS notation requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note on sustained combustibility (not adopted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Note 2 from beneath Table 2.6.1 of Rev. 7 (stating liquids with flash point >35 °C and ≤60 °C need not be classified as non‑flammable for some regulatory purposes if negative sustained combustibility test L.2 results) was requested by commenters but not adopted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA determined incorporating this note would reduce workplace protections given variable workplace conditions (e.g., heating above flash point) and therefore did not incorporate the note into the HCS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aerosols not classified as flammable solids (Appendix B.7 Note 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A new Note 2 following Table B.7.1 states that aerosols should not be classified as flammable solids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aligns Appendix B.7 with Rev. 7 and was finalized as proposed; OSHA received no comments opposing this addition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification based on tested physical form (self-heating solids)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification of solid chemicals must be based on tests performed on the chemicals as presented (i.e., in the physical form supplied or transported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a chemical is presented for supply or transport in a physical form different from that which was tested and that new form is likely to materially alter performance in a classification test, classification must be based on testing of the chemical in the new form. This note was added to Appendix B.11 for consistency with other physical hazards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 3 criterion for chemicals emitting flammable gases in contact with water
rubrics_metrics.description: The criterion in Table B.12.1 for Category 3 is that the maximum rate of evolution of the flammable gas is greater than 1 liter per kilogram of chemical per hour (i.e., remove “equal to or”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change aligns the classification criterion with the corresponding Test N.5 in the UN Manual of Tests and Criteria and Rev.7; OSHA preliminarily determined it would not affect worker protections and finalized the change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oxidizing solids: allow Test O.1 or O.3
rubrics_metrics.description: Oxidizing solids may be classified using either Test O.1 or the newer Test O.3 (Gravimetric tests for oxidizing solids).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because Test O.3 uses a calcium peroxide reference mixture (less hazardous and more available), OSHA allows either test and notes that data from existing classifications based on Test O.1 can still be used so no new testing is required for substances previously classified using O.1. OSHA also updated Note 1 to Table B.14.1 to reflect related IMB code revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Known experience may take precedence over negative test results (oxidizing solids)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there is a difference between test results and known experience showing a chemical to be oxidizing, judgements based on known experience take precedence over negative test results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA's B.14.3.3 requires producers to disclose oxidizing hazards if producer experience indicates such hazards even when tests are negative. Cal/OSHA suggested alternate wording but OSHA retained the substance of the requirement; further discussion of expert judgement is referenced in B.2 (flammable gases) summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: HCS scope excludes consumer product labeling exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA did not adopt a Rev.7 note that would allow omission of the corrosive-to-metals pictogram for finished consumer products because the HCS applies to workplace use, not consumer products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA concluded the labeling provisions referenced in the GHS note were not applicable to the HCS and finalized the decision not to add the note to Appendix B.16.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add desensitized explosives hazard class (Appendix B.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: A new physical hazard class for desensitized explosives is added (Appendix B.17) to provide definitions, classification criteria, additional classification considerations, and references to relevant UN test methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The new hazard class aligns with Rev.7; desensitized explosives are labeled with a flame pictogram (not the explosive bomb) and have tailored precautionary statements. OSHA mostly adopted GHS language but made editorial/regulatory edits (e.g., 'should'→'shall' in places, 'manufacturer/supplier' → 'manufacturers, importers, and distributors'), allowed use of literature data, and removed transport-only classification text. Decision logics from the GHS are not included in regulatory text but may be used in guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Rev.4 vs Rev.6 citations for incorporated UN documents
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA retains a generic citation to ST/SG/AC.10 where compliance with Rev.4 or Rev.6 is allowed and inserts specific citations to ST/SG/AC.10/11/Rev.6 where only Rev.6 is allowed for compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach allows flexibility where both versions are acceptable but requires Rev.6 citation where new Rev.6 text has no Rev.4 counterpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label content must follow Appendix C (paragraph (f)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph (f)(2) requires the chemical manufacturer, importer, or distributor to ensure that the information provided on the label is in accordance with Appendix C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix C provides hazard statements, signal words, pictograms, and precautionary statements for prevention, response, storage, and disposal, plus general labeling instructions. Labels must bear the information specified in Appendix C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure C.1: exclamation mark pictogram may be used for HNOC (non-mandatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise Figure C.1 to include “HNOC (non-mandatory)” as a hazard identified by the exclamation point pictogram; use of the exclamation mark pictogram for HNOCs is permissive, not mandatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change aligns with Health Canada to permit an exclamation mark pictogram to be used for HNOCs so U.S. and Canadian requirements can be met concurrently; OSHA also added desensitized explosives under the flame pictogram in Figure C.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: C.2.3.3: exclamation pictogram for HNOC conditional text
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow the exclamation mark pictogram to be used for HNOCs if the words “Hazard Not Otherwise Classified” or the letters “HNOC” appear below the pictogram on the label.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text related to transport of hazardous chemicals was relocated to paragraph (f)(5)(iii) to consolidate transport instructions; the C.2.3.3 revision implements the HNOC pictogram allowance with the required accompanying legend.

rubrics_metrics.name: C.2.3.4: pictogram may appear only once on a label
rubrics_metrics.description: Because any pictogram may appear only once on a label, if multiple hazards require use of the same pictogram, it may not be repeated a second time on the label.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This addresses situations where the exclamation mark pictogram would otherwise be used for both an HNOC and another hazard; OSHA finalized a new paragraph specifying this limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: C.2.4.7: minor textual variations in precautionary statements allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Precautionary statements may contain minor textual variations (e.g., spelling variations, synonyms, or other equivalent terms) as long as those variations assist communication without diluting or compromising the safety advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any such variations must be used consistently throughout the label and SDS. The provision is permissive (not mandatory) so preparers may retain default Appendix C wording; OSHA expects software can be updated to apply variations consistently. Cal/OSHA objections were considered but OSHA finalized C.2.4.7 to allow minor variations.

rubrics_metrics.name: C.2.4.10: prioritization/combination of medical response precautionary statements
rubrics_metrics.description: When substances/mixtures are classified for multiple hazards that trigger multiple medical response precautionary statements, a system of prioritization and combination is permitted to reduce redundancy on labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA clarified that: (a) If the same medical response statement is triggered multiple times, the label need only include one statement reflecting the response at the highest level with the greatest urgency, and it should always be combined with at least one route of exposure or symptom 'IF' statement. (b) Combination of medical response statements for multiple routes is allowed (but not required) when the same medical response applies. (c) The specific pair of statements “Get medical advice/attention if you feel unwell” and “Get immediate medical advice/attention,” if both applicable, must both appear separately on the label (OSHA changed required wording from “should” to “must” for this provision). OSHA also noted that nothing in C.2.4.10 changes C.2.2's requirement that all applicable hazard statements must appear on the label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency between label and SDS precautionary statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Labels must bear the information specified in Appendix C and precautionary statements in the SDS must be in accordance with paragraph (f) and the allocation rules in Appendix C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions were raised about whether prioritized/combined medical response statements on a label may be represented similarly in the SDS; OSHA's framing of Appendix C and paragraph (f) indicates alignment requirements between label and SDS wording and allocation.
